paths.description: Homepage: primary news discovery template and newsletter entry; tested desktop/mobile, preferences, performance, privacy and memory.
Nieuws section: representative section/listing template and navigation hierarchy.
Current free article: core reading journey, metadata, media, responsive layout and recommendations.
Empty search: primary retrieval form and empty initial state.
Search for “Belgie”: submitted query and populated results state.
Video listing: rich-media template and explicit-play affordances.
Account entry: authentication/recovery surface; redirect reached a 406 blocked-login state.
Invalid route: representative HTTP/error recovery state.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and dark mobile captures are pixel-equivalent in appearance; the probe reports colorScheme "normal", and captured CSS contains no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and supply preference-driven light/dark surface, text, border, and browser-chrome colors, using light-dark() or a prefers-color-scheme fallback.

findings.summary: Continuous ticker and pulse animations continue under reduced-motion.
findings.evidence: The normal and prefers-reduced-motion probes both report the same 13 running animations, including 273,620 ms ticker/swap animations; captured CSS contains no prefers-reduced-motion rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop auto-moving tickers and repeated pulse effects and replace them with a static state.

findings.summary: Route changes do not use cross-document View Transitions.
findings.evidence: DOM/CSS captures across the home, section and article templates contain no view-transition declaration, so full-page news navigation swaps abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Add @view-transition { navigation: auto } with stable view-transition-name values for shared header and article imagery, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Sticky navigation is not implemented with scroll-state-aware CSS.
findings.evidence: Captured CSS uses fixed/relative header class toggles but contains no scroll-state container query; the long article has 11,209 px of content with no declarative reading-progress affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state queries or a lightweight declarative progress indicator so long-article chrome responds to reading position.

findings.summary: Templates rely on viewport media queries rather than component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: CSS from home and article templates contains no @container or container-type declaration, despite cards being reused in hero, rail, list and mobile contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Establish containment on reusable card/list regions and move size-dependent card styling to container queries.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target treatment is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: The home focus probe reports most links with outline-style none and no box shadow; multiple visible links are only 12–20 px high. The article template has a stronger 2 px focus outline, showing cross-template inconsistency.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a consistent high-contrast :focus-visible ring across templates and provide at least 24×24 CSS px targets, preferably 44×44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The mobile homepage has a poor layout-stability result.
findings.evidence: The 360×800 layout capture measured CLS 0.160156 with a single shift at about 5.08 s; Lighthouse also measured cold-load LCP at 3.7 s on home and 4.2 s on the article.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve space for late advertising/personalisation modules and prioritise the actual LCP image while deferring non-critical work.

findings.summary: The homepage loads a disproportionate network payload before the user asks for rich media.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 143 requests and 7,769,884 transferred bytes. Seven video-segment requests contributed 4,388,646 bytes, while scripts contributed 2,445,626 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not fetch video segments until the player is near the viewport or activated; delay advertising, experimentation and analytics scripts by user value and priority.

findings.summary: Third-party and duplicated script work dominates page delivery.
findings.evidence: The article HAR recorded 72 scripts and 2,749,557 script bytes; the live script inventory includes repeated pexi.js loads plus advertising, survey, experimentation and analytics libraries.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory third-party value, remove duplicate loader instances, conditionally load integrations, and apply performance budgets per template.

findings.summary: Some controls and content images lack robust accessible names.
findings.evidence: The home probe found one unlabelled visible input; the input inventory shows the required newsletter email field has no label or aria-label. The image audit found 100 home images without alt values, including story imagery.
findings.suggestedFix: Label newsletter/search inputs programmatically and give meaningful story images concise alt text, using empty alt only when adjacent link text makes the image decorative.

findings.summary: Heading structure skips levels and differs between templates.
findings.evidence: The article probe jumps from H1 to an H6 newsletter heading before H2; Lighthouse also flags non-sequential heading order in the consent surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use headings for document hierarchy rather than visual size and keep levels sequential in shared widgets and the consent experience.

findings.summary: Article assets are not consistently dimensioned or responsive.
findings.evidence: The article image audit found 8 images without dimensions, 12 oversized images, 53 without srcset and 29 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit width/height or aspect-ratio for every image and provide responsive AVIF/WebP sources sized to each card slot.

findings.summary: The consent journey prevents back/forward cache restoration and raises browser issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons around Cache-Control: no-store and a DevTools cookie issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep no-store scoped to genuinely sensitive responses and ensure the consent handoff does not unnecessarily disqualify the content page from BFCache.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP configuration weakens otherwise strong transport security.
findings.evidence: Headers include HSTS, nosniff and X-Frame-Options, but CSP permits unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval. The cookie audit found 22 of 24 cookies lacking Secure and many SameSite=None cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Move to nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval and mark all HTTPS cookies Secure; use Lax/Strict unless cross-site delivery is essential.

findings.summary: The default page has an extensive advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: The tracker capture saw 50 third-party origins and 11 known tracker domains. The HAR classified 137 of 143 requests and 7.66 MB of 7.77 MB as cross-origin.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors to those with demonstrated user value, gate non-essential collection on consent, batch analytics, and proxy or self-host essential static assets where practical.

findings.summary: The tested login path is blocked and offers no passkey route.
findings.evidence: Navigating to /login ends on a 406 “Inlogpoging geblokkeerd” page. It instructs users to go back and use an emailed six-digit code, but presents no actionable return link or phishing-resistant passkey option.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a direct recovery action on the blocked state and offer WebAuthn/passkeys as the primary sign-in method, retaining email code as recovery.

findings.summary: Core news content is not present in the raw no-JavaScript response for a generic crawler.
findings.evidence: Discoverability fetches for home and article each saw about 8 KB of raw HTML, only 3 content tokens, no title/H1/description and 0% rendered-word coverage because the response is a privacy-gate shell.
findings.suggestedFix: Return server-rendered title, metadata, navigation and article body in the initial response; enhance consent and personalisation without replacing core content.

findings.summary: The install manifest is not backed by an active offline experience.
findings.evidence: The home and article probes find a manifest but no controlling service worker; no offline fallback is available for a news product whose read path benefits from flaky-network resilience.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a narrowly scoped service worker with an offline shell and cached recently read articles, while keeping live content network-first.

findings.summary: Newsletter email inputs omit autocomplete hints.
findings.evidence: The home input inventory shows both email fields with an empty autocomplete value, and the required compact newsletter field has no programmatic label.
findings.suggestedFix: Set autocomplete="email" and provide persistent programmatic labels for newsletter fields.

findings.summary: The account entry flow dead-ends in the audited environment.
findings.evidence: The 406 blocked-login page contains instructions but no button or link back to the alternative code flow, so the user cannot continue from the state presented.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a visible “Continue with email code” action, preserve the original return URL, and expose account/cancellation recovery without requiring browser-back guesswork.

findings.summary: Article recommendations ship oversized and legacy media.
findings.evidence: The article image audit found 12 oversized images, 53 without responsive sources and 29 legacy-format assets, including 480 px GIF/JPEG thumbnails displayed at 112 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive variants at card dimensions and avoid animated GIF for preview motion.

findings.summary: Background video and vendor work consumes megabytes without an explicit play action.
findings.evidence: The home probe found no autoplay media element, yet the HAR downloaded seven HLS segments totalling 4.39 MB and contacted 50 third-party origins during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritise and condition video/ad requests on viewport proximity, explicit playback, consent and idle time; cancel work when hidden.

findings.summary: Third-party media cost is disproportionate to a news homepage first view.
findings.evidence: Cross-origin resources account for 7.66 MB of 7.77 MB transferred on the homepage, including video, player, tag-manager, advertising and experimentation payloads.
findings.suggestedFix: Set per-template third-party and media budgets and enforce them in delivery, loading only the lightest assets needed for the visible story list.

findings.summary: The site deliberately blocks major AI agents and exposes no structured action interface.
findings.evidence: robots.txt disallows GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Google-Extended, Perplexity and many peers; captured DOM has no WebMCP/agent-tool surface, although article JSON-LD is strong.
findings.suggestedFix: If agent reach is desired, define an explicit AI crawler policy and expose safe search/article capabilities through structured tools while retaining authorization boundaries.

taskList.title: Stop eager background video and rationalise third-party delivery
Restore server-rendered core content through the privacy handoff
Reserve late module space and improve LCP priority
Repair labels, headings, focus rings and touch targets
Make login recovery actionable and add passkeys
Adopt container queries, scroll-state UI and view transitions
Define intentional agent access and structured capabilities
